newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SERVICE INDUSTRY BULLISH ON SALES, JOBS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SERVICE INDUSTRY BULLISH ON SALES, JOBS.

text.p: Cyclical prospects for the service industry are now better than a year ago and many service sector firms expect to add new jobs as their sales grow, the Confederation of Finnish Servcice Industries said on Tuesday.
"Cyclical expectations in the private service sectors are somewhat better than a year ago," the confederation said.

About half of service sector firms now expect the business cycle to improve and about half expect it to remain unchanged. One year ago, one third of the companies expected the cyclical outlook to worsen.
Among services seeing better times ahead were financing, insurance, trade and commerce and data programming -- the last having the most positive outlook, the confederation said.
More than half of all the companies surveyed expected sales to grow in 1997.
Half of insurance companies expected premium income to grow but only just over one tenth of banks expected a pick-up in credit extension.
"The improvement in employment in private services will continue this year," the confederation said.

Wholesalers, retailers, hotels, restaurants, health care, advertising, data services, travel and tourism, real estate and maintenance companies were among branches expecting to hire more staff this year.
But the number of employees in banking and financing would go on falling.
Service sector companies expected profitability to improve in 1997 for the fourth year running, especially in financing and insurance, the confederation said.
The survey was conducted late in 1996 and covered 820 service sector companies employing a total of 165,000 people.
